members.title: PM to meet NCP delegation led by Nahid Islam at the Secretariat
members.lead: The National Citizen Party (NCP), formed by the student leaders who led the July mass uprising, is sitting for a dialogue with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today, Monday. The dialogue will take place at 1:00 pm at the prime minister's office in the Cabinet Division at the Secretariat. Three leaders of the party, including NCP convener and chief whip of the opposition in the National Parliament Nahid Islam, will participate in the dialogue. The other two are NCP member secretary and member of parliament, Akhtar Hossain, and NCP senior joint convener and member of parliament Hasnat Abdullah. In the wake of subversive activities by the Awami League, whose activities are banned, the prime minister called upon anti-fascist political parties in the National Parliament on 18 November to come together on one platform. .Dialogue with the PM today, NCP to present two conditions for unity. Leader of the opposition in parliament and Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur Rahman also highlighted the necessity of unity among the parties that day. The prime minister and the leader of the opposition spoke privately on the matter. In continuation of those developments, the prime minister’s dialogue with political parties begins today. As the first party, NCP leaders are sitting for talks with the head of government this afternoon. With the goal of national unity, the prime minister is scheduled to hold successive discussions with other parties, including Jamaat. . The NCP delegation will sit for discussions with the prime minister at the Secretariat at 1:00 pm today. The delegation will include Nahid Islam, Akhtar Hossain, and Hasnat Abdullah. Sarwar Tusher, joint convener, NCP . NCP joint convener Sarwar Tusher told Prothom Alo this morning that the NCP delegation will sit for discussions with the prime minister at the Secretariat at 1:00 pm today. members.title: Sought roadmap from PM to deal with AL, India issues: Nahid Islam
members.lead: National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam has sought a long-term roadmap from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on how the government plans to deal with the activities-banned Awami League and India in the future. He told journalists this after a meeting with the prime minister at the Secretariat on Monday. The NCP delegation, led by Nahid Islam, included Member Secretary Akhter Hossen, Senior Joint Convener Hasnat Abdullah and Joint Convener Aktar Hossain. Nahid spoke to journalists after the meeting and a lunch hosted by the prime minister. The discussion between the prime minister and NCP leaders lasted 35 minutes. The NCP convener said, “The head of government has called for unity. We have said that there should be a foundation and a roadmap outlining what is needed to strengthen this unity further and bring together all forces that took part in the July uprising and the struggle against fascism to move Bangladesh forward. “This cannot be limited to December alone. We will have to deal with the Awami League and India issues in the coming days. Therefore, we need a long-term roadmap.” Nahid Islam said the meeting covered the current situation in the country, contemporary politics and various crises. He said the law and order situation had deteriorated significantly in recent days, severely affecting public safety. He also referred to what he described as acts of violence and arson by the ousted authoritarian and fascist Awami League. . According to Nahid, the prime minister expressed his concerns about the current situation and called on political parties to remain united on the issues of fascism and the July uprising. . The discussion focused on how to overcome the situation and whether political unity was possible, he added.
